source: Observed on the service (commit 55cf875, 2026-10-15) and written by hand, because the service's OpenAPI describes none of its response bodies. Fields not listed here exist but are outside the rules.

conventions.success: HTTP 200 with {request_id, data, warnings, partial, server_time}. The payload is `data`.
conventions.error: {request_id, error: {code, message, retryable, retry_after_seconds, details}, server_time}. Schema violations are HTTP 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and `details` naming each bad field.
conventions.money: Response amounts end in `_minor`: integers in minor units (1/100 of the currency unit). Request amounts and quantities are decimal strings in currency units.
conventions.enum_case: Request enums are UPPER-CASE (BANK, FUND, DEPOSIT). Responses return the same values lower-case (bank, fund, deposit).
conventions.version: Every record has `version`: 1 when created, +1 on every change. Updating or archiving requires the record's current version.
conventions.archive: Archiving is soft. The record leaves the list endpoints and the summary; archiving or touching it again behaves as if it does not exist.
conventions.batch: holdings.batch_upsert and transactions.batch_upsert need a `client_request_id` and take 1 to 500 items. Items without an id create records; items with an id and the current version update them.
conventions.ids: account_id, holding_id and transaction_id are opaque strings returned by earlier calls.
conventions.scoping: Every call acts as one user and only sees that user's records.

Account.name: string
Account.account_type: lower-case: brokerage | fund | bank | crypto | other

Holding.name: string
Holding.asset_type: lower-case: stock | etf | fund | lof | reit | bond | cash | crypto | other
Holding.current_price: number or null (unit price; set it with metadata.current_price in the request)
Holding.unrealized_profit_minor: integer or null (null when average_cost is missing)
Holding.valuation_status: "priced" when a price is known, otherwise "estimated"

Transaction.holding_id: not echoed back; sent only in requests
Transaction.transaction_type: lower-case: buy | sell | dividend | deposit | withdrawal | fee | interest | transfer | other
Transaction.amount_minor: integer (keeps the sign that was sent)

LedgerSummary.other_fields: records, goals, allocation, categories, generated_at and price_refresh also exist; the rules do not cover them

operations.accounts.upsert: data = Account. Without account_id it creates; with account_id and the current version it updates.
